fields.mechanism: Heparin coating provides surface anticoagulant activity that inhibits fibrin and platelet adhesion.
fields.intervention: Apply a heparin‑based anti‑fouling coating to marine vessel hulls or offshore pipeline interiors to prevent biofouling and scale buildup.
fields.expected_effect: Reduced biofilm and mineral deposit formation, maintaining fluid flow and lowering drag/pressure loss.
fields.falsification_test: Field study deploying coated vs uncoated hull panels/pipeline sections in identical marine conditions and measuring fouling mass and flow resistance over a 30‑day period.

fields.mechanism: Heparin coating provides an anticoagulant surface that inhibits thrombus formation, leading to longer failure‑free survival.
fields.intervention: Apply a permanent, covalently bonded hydrophilic polymer (e.g., PEG brush) to the catheter lumen and external surface to create a passive, non‑fouling interface that physically repels protein and cellular adhesion, thereby preventing clot buildup without active heparin.
fields.expected_effect: Sustained ≥300 mL/min flow for weeks post‑insertion with reduced occlusion risk, matching or exceeding heparin‑coated performance while avoiding systemic anticoagulant exposure and infection risk.
fields.falsification_test: In a controlled in‑vitro blood loop, compare flow rate decay, pressure rise, and thrombus mass over 30 days among uncoated catheters, heparin‑coated catheters, and the PEG‑coated catheters; the hypothesis is falsified if PEG‑coated catheters do not demonstrate flow preservation comparable to heparin‑coated devices.

fields.mechanism: Anticoagulant heparin coating on the catheter surface reduces thrombus formation and occlusion.
fields.intervention: Apply a continuous heparin-bonded polymer coating to the inner lumen and external surface of the tunneled hemodialysis catheter.
fields.expected_effect: Maintains ≥300 mL/min blood flow for weeks post‑insertion with no increase in infection risk.

fields.mechanism: Anticoagulant surface provided by heparin coating that inhibits thrombus formation on catheter lumen.
fields.intervention: Apply a heparin coating to the inner lumen of the tunneled catheter and embed a low‑intensity ultrasonic transducer in the catheter wall to deliver periodic acoustic energy that synergistically disrupts platelet adhesion and enhances heparin activity.
fields.expected_effect: Sustained ≥300 mL/min blood flow with markedly reduced catheter occlusion over weeks without raising infection risk.
fields.falsification_test: Randomized bench‑scale flow loop comparing (a) heparin‑coated catheters alone vs (b) heparin‑coated catheters with ultrasonic actuation, measuring time to >50 % flow reduction under standardized clot‑forming conditions.

fields.mechanism: Anticoagulant heparin surface reduces thrombus formation within the catheter lumen, preserving flow patency.
fields.intervention: Apply a covalently bonded heparin coating to the inner lumen and external surface of the tunneled hemodialysis catheter to create a continuous antithrombotic interface.
fields.expected_effect: Sustained ≥300 mL/min blood flow for weeks post‑insertion with no rise in infection incidence, due to inhibition of fibrin/platelet deposition that causes occlusion.
fields.falsification_test: Conduct a blinded, randomized clinical trial comparing heparin‑coated catheters to identical uncoated catheters, measuring time to first flow‑limiting occlusion and quantifying intraluminal thrombus via ultrasound; a lack of statistically significant patency improvement falsifies the mechanism.
